engagement_summary.substance_name: Bovine lactoferrin produced by a modified strain of Komagataella phaffii (ALLGLF)
engagement_summary.notifier: All G Co Holdings Pty Limited (agent: Vireo Advisors, LLC / Jo Anne Shatkin, Ph.D.)
engagement_summary.production_method: Precision fermentation using genetically modified K. phaffii strain Ppas_337 with introduced bovine lactoferrin gene
engagement_summary.source_organism: Komagataella phaffii (strain Ppas_337, derived from BG11 lineage of NRRL Y-11430)
intended_uses: Sports and functional foods and beverages
engagement_summary.target_population: General population including infants and children; adults; vulnerable subpopulations addressed in dietary exposure section
engagement_summary.submission_completeness_note: Submission includes Parts 1–7, FDA Form 3667, cover letter, and a January 2026 amendment responding to FDA questions. The input was smart-truncated; allergenicity LC-MS/MS results, Part 6.4 summary, and full Part 7 references were not fully available for review.

categorical_eligibility.basis: Submission is structured as a GRAS notice under 21 CFR §170 Subpart E, based on scientific procedures. K. phaffii is an established expression host for food ingredients with multiple prior successful GRNs. Bovine lactoferrin has multiple prior 'no questions' GRNs from cow's milk sources.

scope_clarity.notes: Food categories and use levels are provided in Tables 1 and 6. 'Probiotic drinks' category was flagged by FDA and confirmed removed in January 2026 amendment. Technical function is as a protein ingredient/nutritional component.

existing_regulatory_status.prior_gras_notices: GRNs 67, 77, 130, 464, 465, 669 (cow's milk-derived lactoferrin, all 'no questions'); GRN 1219 (recombinant bLF from K. phaffii by Turtle Tree, reported 'no questions' publicly but listed as pending at submission date)
existing_regulatory_status.food_additive_approvals: 21 CFR 573.587 cited for animal feed context; confirmed by notifier as non-applicable to human food safety conclusion
existing_regulatory_status.notes: EFSA granted K. phaffii QPS status for production purposes. Multiple prior K. phaffii-derived food ingredient GRNs (GRNs 204, 737, 967, 1001, 1025, 1056, 1104, 1142) received no questions.

potential_safety_signals.signal: Non-native glycosylation pattern (phosphomannose glycans; absence of hybrid and complex glycans)
potential_safety_signals.evidence: LC-MS/MS glycan analysis shows ALLGLF lacks hybrid/complex glycans present in native bLF and contains phosphomannose glycans typical of yeast expression. Submission argues differences are negligible based on K. phaffii QPS status and GRN 1104 precedent.
potential_safety_signals.recommended_action: Confirm whether phosphomannose glycans have been evaluated for immunogenicity in relevant populations; cross-reference with GRN 1219 FDA review of same structural feature.

potential_safety_signals.signal: Residual K. phaffii host cell proteins in final product
potential_safety_signals.evidence: LC-MS/MS analysis of three batches was conducted to characterize residual host cell proteins. Table 12 shows identified protein abundance; full results appear truncated in the reviewed input.
potential_safety_signals.recommended_action: Verify that full residual host cell protein identity and allergenicity screening results are present in the untruncated submission.

potential_safety_signals.signal: Antibody response to bovine lactoferrin observed in human clinical study
potential_safety_signals.evidence: Peterson et al. (2024) randomized trial detected significant anti-lactoferrin antibody response to bLF at 3.4 g/day over 28 days. No clinical allergy or adverse events were reported.
potential_safety_signals.recommended_action: Assess whether the immunogenicity finding warrants further characterization, particularly for repeat/high-dose consumers and atopic individuals.

identity_and_characterization.summary: ALLGLF is extensively characterized relative to native bLF using SDS-PAGE, LC-MS/MS amino acid sequencing, glycan analysis, iron binding, isoelectric point, circular dichroism, and DSC. Minor glycosylation differences (phosphomannose; absence of hybrid/complex glycans) are acknowledged. Characterization data are published in Food Hydrocolloids (Cavallo et al., 2025).

strengths.observation: Seven independent physicochemical parameters compared head-to-head between ALLGLF and commercial bLF, providing a comprehensive structural similarity package.
Characterization peer-reviewed and published in an open-access journal, satisfying general availability requirements for this data.

gaps.title: Pepsin digestibility data not identified
gaps.observation: No pepsin digestibility assay for ALLGLF was identified in the reviewed text. For a novel protein with non-native glycosylation, digestibility data support allergenicity conclusions. The submission relies on bioinformatic screening and host organism history but does not appear to include a digestibility study.

gaps.title: Full allergenicity LC-MS/MS results truncated
gaps.observation: Section 6.3 and Table 12 were truncated in the input provided. The full residual host cell protein allergenicity screening results should be verified in the complete submission document.

manufacturing_process.summary: The manufacturing process is described with a process diagram (Figure 8) covering fermentation through purification. Production strain construction (Ppas_337), genetic stability over 87 generations, absence of antibiotic resistance genes, and absence of viable cells in final product are documented. Processing aids are stated to be food-grade and GRAS.

strengths.observation: Genetic construction of Ppas_337 documented including AOX1 deletion, introduced DNA origins (Bos taurus, S. cerevisiae), and whole-genome sequencing confirmation.
Three independent production batches analyzed with consistent results demonstrating process reproducibility.

gaps.title: Specific processing aids and reagents not fully enumerated in reviewed text
gaps.observation: The narrative states all processing aids are food-grade and GRAS but does not appear to enumerate each reagent, solvent, and chromatography media used. Full enumeration is needed to confirm no residual process-related contaminants of concern.

gaps.title: Residual methanol characterization not addressed
gaps.observation: K. phaffii uses methanol as inducer/carbon source. No specification limit or measured residual methanol level in the final product was identified in the reviewed text. Methanol residue in fermentation-derived food ingredients is a known process-related contaminant concern.

dietary_exposure.summary: Estimated dietary intake is calculated using proposed use levels across food categories (Table 7), with background lactoferrin exposure from bovine milk addressed (Table 8) and cumulative exposure including other GRAS-notified sources (Table 9). Subpopulations including infants and children appear to be addressed. The methodology section references NHANES or equivalent data sources.

strengths.observation: Background bovine lactoferrin exposure from milk consumption is quantified and integrated into cumulative exposure estimates alongside ALLGLF.
Conservative approach using 90th percentile consumers-only intake values acknowledged, with infant and age-stratified analysis included.

gaps.title: Dietary exposure methodology detail truncated
gaps.observation: The methodology section is referenced but not fully reproduced in the reviewed input. Whether aggregate total-sample intake or eaters-only distributions were used as the primary conservative estimate cannot be confirmed from reviewed text alone.

gaps.title: 'Probiotic drinks' category originally included
gaps.observation: FDA identified 'probiotic drinks' in Tables 1 and 6. Notifier confirmed removal in January 2026 amendment. The original intake calculation may have included this category; it should be confirmed that the EDI tables were updated to reflect removal.

safety_data.summary: The safety data package for bLF is extensive, including acute, sub-acute (14-day), 4-week, 13-week subchronic, and chronic (40–65 week) oral toxicity studies in rats with NOAEL >2000 mg/kg/day. Human clinical data at doses up to 9 g/day show no adverse effects. Read-across from bLF to ALLGLF is supported by demonstrated structural similarity. A 100-fold safety factor is applied.

strengths.observation: Chronic rodent feeding studies up to 65 weeks at 5% dietary bLF with no adverse effects; NOAEL >2000 mg/kg/day independently established across multiple studies.
Human clinical safety data at high doses (up to 9 g/day in adults; up to 833 mg/day in infants) with no significant adverse events provides direct human relevance.
28-day oral toxicity and immunotoxicity study of recombinant lactoferrin produced in K. phaffii (rhLF, Effera) with NOAEL 2000 mg/kg/day provides direct relevance to recombinant production.

gaps.title: Genotoxicity data for ALLGLF not identified
gaps.observation: No genotoxicity studies (Ames test, chromosomal aberration, or in vitro micronucleus) for ALLGLF or bLF were identified in the reviewed text. For a novel precision fermentation protein, a standard genotoxicity battery is expected. Reliance on read-across alone may not be sufficient.

gaps.title: Safety data specific to ALLGLF limited; read-across to bLF and rhLF
gaps.observation: Safety studies are conducted with bLF or rhLF (a different recombinant product). ALLGLF-specific toxicology is not presented. The structural similarity case is well-made, but the non-native glycosylation pattern is a distinguishing feature that may warrant at least a subacute study with ALLGLF itself.

gaps.title: Reproductive and developmental toxicity data not identified
gaps.observation: No reproductive or developmental toxicity studies for bLF or ALLGLF were identified. Given the proposed use in foods consumed by pregnant women and infants/young children, and the broad use categories, the absence of this data element warrants attention.

general_availability.summary: The primary characterization data are published in Food Hydrocolloids (Cavallo et al., 2025) as open-access. Safety data for bLF reference peer-reviewed publications and prior GRAS submissions. The Peterson et al. (2024) rhLF studies are cited; their publication status should be verified.

strengths.observation: ALLGLF characterization data published open-access in Food Hydrocolloids, satisfying the public availability requirement for that dataset.
Core bLF safety data (Yamauchi et al., 2000; Tamano et al., 2008) are peer-reviewed published studies widely available to qualified experts.

gaps.title: Publication status of Peterson et al. (2024) studies unclear
gaps.observation: Peterson et al. (2024) is cited for multiple key safety studies (14-day, 28-day toxicity, human clinical trial). If these are unpublished or preprint-only at filing date, they can corroborate but cannot independently establish the GRAS conclusion. Publication status should be confirmed.

general_acceptance.summary: Strong signals of general acceptance exist: EFSA QPS status for K. phaffii, multiple prior K. phaffii food ingredient GRNs with no questions, EFSA safety opinion on bLF including infant formula, and the closely analogous GRN 1219 (recombinant bLF from K. phaffii) reportedly receiving a no-questions letter. No identified scientific controversy regarding bLF safety.

strengths.observation: EFSA QPS status for K. phaffii and EFSA 2012 scientific opinion on bLF safety including infant formula use represent authoritative international body endorsement.
Eight prior K. phaffii-derived food ingredient GRNs with no-questions outcomes, including GRN 1219 for the same substance (recombinant bLF), support broad expert acceptance of the platform.

gaps.title: GRN 1219 status relied upon but listed as pending at filing
gaps.observation: GRN 1219 is cited as supporting precedent but was officially listed as pending in the FDA inventory at filing. The notifier acknowledges this discrepancy. Its evidentiary weight as general acceptance support is qualified until official FDA disposition is confirmed.

conditions_of_use.summary: Food categories and use levels are specified in Tables 1 and 6, with numerical use levels (e.g., mg/serving, mg/100g). Technical function is identified as a protein ingredient. The 'probiotic drinks' category was removed via amendment. Target population encompasses general population including vulnerable subgroups.

strengths.observation: Use levels are provided in quantitative terms across each food category, enabling exposure calculation and safety margin assessment.

gaps.title: Infant formula exclusion not explicitly stated
gaps.observation: Prior K. phaffii GRNs (e.g., GRN 967) explicitly exclude infant formula. The reviewed text does not clearly state whether ALLGLF is intended for or excluded from infant formula. Given infant-specific exposure analysis, this boundary should be explicit in the conditions of use.

regulatory_submission.summary: The submission includes all seven parts of a GRAS notice, FDA Form 3667 with dual certification (agent and notifier), and a substantive amendment responding to FDA questions. Certification is provided by both Jo Anne Shatkin (agent) and Jared Raynes (All G). The submission appears structurally complete.

strengths.observation: Both the notifier (Jared Raynes, All G) and the agent (Jo Anne Shatkin, Vireo Advisors) provide signed certifications of completeness, balance, and accuracy.
Proactive January 2026 amendment responding to FDA questions demonstrates engagement and addresses the animal feed regulatory citation and probiotic drinks category issues.
